title: Simultaneous finite algebra and module models over a Noetherian local subring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, so $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $C$ be a finitely presented commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and let $M$ be a finitely presented $C$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There exist a unital subring $R_0\subseteq R$, a finitely presented commutative $R_0$-algebra $C_0$, and a finitely presented $C_0$-module $M_0$ with the following properties. The ring $R_0$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=R_0\cap\mathfrak m$, is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and is essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. In particular $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated. There are an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:R\otimes_{R_0}C_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ and a $C$-linear isomorphism $\beta:C\otimes_{C_0}M_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, where $C_0\to C$ is $c\mapsto\alpha(1\otimes c)$. Consequently the canonical balanced map $R\otimes_{R_0}M_0\to M$, $r\otimes x\mapsto r\,\beta(1\otimes x)$, is an $R$-linear isomorphism compatible with the $C$-actions through $\alpha$. Tensor products have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No flatness of $C$ or $M$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: the local essentially finite type subring A_0 and simultaneous models B_0,N_0 before I=m_{A_0}A is chosen.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] choose $C\cong R[X_1,\ldots,X_d]/(F_1,\ldots,F_e)$, and by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] choose $C^a\xrightarrow{H}C^b\to M\to0$. Lift every entry of the finite matrix $H$ to a polynomial $h_{ij}(X)$ over $R$, and list their finitely many coefficients as $u_1,\ldots,u_t$. To include these coefficients in an algebra-presentation core, use the equivalent presentation
$$C\cong R[X_1,\ldots,X_d,Y_1,\ldots,Y_t]/(F_1,\ldots,F_e,Y_1-u_1,\ldots,Y_t-u_t).$$
Indeed evaluation $Y_l\mapsto u_l$ and the inclusion of the $X$-variables are inverse on the two quotients: they fix $R,X_i$, and $Y_l=u_l$ in the augmented quotient. Empty variable, relation and matrix index sets are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] to the augmented presentation. Its coefficient subring $D\subseteq R$ is generated over $\mathbf Z$ by the coefficients of the $F_j$ and the $u_l$; the extra coefficients $1,-1$ already lie in the image of $\mathbf Z$. The cited statement gives that $D$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and Noetherian. Write
$$E=D[X,Y]/(F^D_1,\ldots,F^D_e,Y_1-u_1,\ldots,Y_t-u_t).$$
It is finitely presented over $D$, and the canonical map $E\otimes_D R\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ is an algebra isomorphism with the displayed evaluation formulas. The same statement gives the polynomial presentation of $E\otimes_D T$ for every commutative $D$-algebra $T$, without a flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak p=D\cap\mathfrak m$ and $W=D\setminus\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is maximal it is prime, so $W$ is multiplicatively closed. Every $w\in W$ is a unit of $R$: otherwise the proper ideal $(w)$ lies in a maximal ideal, necessarily $\mathfrak m$. Define the unital subring $R_0=\{d/w:d\in D,w\in W\}\subseteq R$. The map $W^{-1}D\to R$, $d/w\mapsto dw^{-1}$, is injective: a fraction mapping to zero has $d=0$ in $R$, hence in the subring $D$. Thus $R_0$ is a localization of $D$. Its ideal $\mathfrak n=R_0\cap\mathfrak m$ consists exactly of fractions whose numerator lies in $\mathfrak p$. A fraction outside $\mathfrak n$ has inverse $w/d\in R_0$. As $1\notin\mathfrak n$, the ideal is proper; all elements outside it are units, so every proper ideal is contained in it. Consequently $\mathfrak n$ is the unique maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text: The ring $D$ is Noetherian by step 2 and $R_0$ is its localization at $W$ by step 3. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] gives that $R_0$ is Noetherian. Since $D$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$, the description $R_0=W^{-1}D$ is precisely essentially finite type in [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], every ideal of $R_0$, in particular $\mathfrak n$, is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text:
Set $C_0=E\otimes_D R_0$. The last clause of [lem-trf-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model], with $T=R_0$, presents $C_0$ as $R_0[X,Y]/(F^{R_0},Y-u)$, so it is finitely presented. Combining the same clause with $T=R$ and the isomorphism of step 2 gives
$$\alpha:R\otimes_{R_0}C_0\xrightarrow{\sim}C.$$
For clarity the tensor identification used here is $R\otimes_{R_0}(E\otimes_D R_0)\cong E\otimes_D R$: $r\otimes(e\otimes s)\mapsto e\otimes rs$, with inverse $e\otimes r\mapsto r\otimes(e\otimes1)$. These formulas respect the balanced relations and are inverse on pure tensors. In particular $c_0\mapsto\alpha(1\otimes c_0)$ sends the classes of $X_i,Y_l$ to their values in $C$.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text: Each $h_{ij}$ has coefficients in $D\subseteq R_0$, so its class gives an entry of a matrix $H_0:C_0^a\to C_0^b$. Define $M_0=\operatorname{coker}H_0$. This is finitely presented by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] over $C_0$ to $C_0^a\to C_0^b\to M_0\to0$, tensoring with $C$. The free-module identifications $C\otimes_{C_0}C_0^q\cong C^q$ send $c\otimes(v_i)$ to $(cv_i)$; their inverses send $(c_i)$ to $\sum_i c_i\otimes e_i$. Since $H_0$ maps to $H$ entrywise, the resulting sequence is $C^a\xrightarrow H C^b\to C\otimes_{C_0}M_0\to0$. Both this module and $M$ are the quotient of $C^b$ by $\operatorname{im}H$; the quotient maps therefore give a $C$-linear isomorphism $\beta:C\otimes_{C_0}M_0\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Only right exactness is used, so no flatness of $C$ or $M$ over $R$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, proof: simultaneous local coefficient-subring models; explicit presentation argument filling the omitted construction.

proof.text:
Using the balanced relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the maps
$$R\otimes_{R_0}M_0\ \longleftrightarrow\ (R\otimes_{R_0}C_0)\otimes_{C_0}M_0,$$
$$r\otimes x\longmapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes x,\qquad(r\otimes c_0)\otimes x\longmapsto r\otimes(c_0x)$$
are well-defined inverse $R$-linear maps. The first composite fixes $r\otimes x$, and the other fixes $(r\otimes c_0)\otimes x$ because $(r\otimes1)\otimes(c_0x)=(r\otimes c_0)\otimes x$. Apply $\alpha$ on the algebra tensor factor and then $\beta$. The composite sends $r\otimes x$ to $r\beta(1\otimes x)$, hence is exactly the required canonical map and is an isomorphism. On the middle tensor product the action of $R\otimes_{R_0}C_0$ is multiplication on its first factor, so after $\alpha$ the maps respect the specified $C$-action.

(2) The coefficient-core leaf applies to that specified presentation; D contains the u_l, is of finite type over Z and Noetherian, E⊗_D R≅C, and the clause holds for any D-algebra T. (3) The elements of W are units of R because R is local; W^{-1}D→R is injective; n=R_0∩m is the unique maximal ideal. (4) Conditions (a)-(c) of lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian hold, and the essentially-finite-type definition is met. (5) C_0=E⊗_D R_0 is finitely presented by the T=R_0 clause; the α associativity formulas were checked. (6) H_0 has entries over D, right exactness needs no flatness, and coker H gives β. (7) The associativity iso and the C_0-linearity of α give exactly r⊗x↦rβ(1⊗x). Edge cases checked: empty data, M=0, C=0, R a field, zero divisors, positive characteristic, and the example R=k[[t]], C=R[x]/(x^2-t). lean.statement: theorem exists_local_algebra_module_noetherian_subring_model (R : Type u) (C : Type v) (M : Type w) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [CommRing C] [Algebra R C] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R C] [AddCommGroup M] [Module C M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R C M] [Module.FinitePresentation C M] : ∃ (R₀ : Subring R) (_ : IsLocalRing R₀), IsNoetherianRing R₀ ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType ℤ R₀ ∧ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀ = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).comap R₀.subtype ∧ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R₀).FG ∧ ∃ (C₀ : Type u) (_ : CommRing C₀) (_ : Algebra R₀ C₀), Algebra.FinitePresentation R₀ C₀ ∧ ∃ (α : R ⊗[R₀] C₀ ≃ₐ[R] C) (_ : Algebra C₀ C), (∀ c₀ : C₀, algebraMap C₀ C c₀ = α (1 ⊗ₜ[R₀] c₀)) ∧ ∃ (M₀ : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M₀) (_ : Module C₀ M₀) (_ : Module R₀ M₀) (_ : IsScalarTower R₀ C₀ M₀), Module.FinitePresentation C₀ M₀ ∧ ∃ (β : C ⊗[C₀] M₀ ≃ₗ[C] M) (γ : R ⊗[R₀] M₀ ≃ₗ[R] M), (∀ (r : R) (x : M₀), γ (r ⊗ₜ[R₀] x) = r • β (1 ⊗ₜ[C₀] x)) ∧ (∀ (c₀ : C₀) (r : R) (x : M₀), γ (r ⊗ₜ[R₀] (c₀ • x)) = α (1 ⊗ₜ[R₀] c₀) • γ (r ⊗ₜ[R₀] x))
